chunks: And Saif ibn ʿAmīrah narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "A man has nothing of the fiṭrah except what would suffice to discharge it for himself alone. Should he give it on her behalf, or should he and his dependents eat it?"
He عليه السلام said: "He gives it to some of his dependents, then the other gives it on behalf of himself; they pass it among themselves, and it thereby counts for all of them as one fiṭrah."

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةِ: zakat al-fiṭrah, the alms due at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.عِيَالُهُ: his dependents or family members under his care
key_terms.فِطْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ: one fiṭrah payment serving collectively in the described case
key_terms.نَفْسِهِ: himself, indicating personal liability or behalf
key_terms.يُؤَدِّي: to discharge or fulfill an obligatory payment
key_terms.يُرَدِّدُونَهَا: they circulate or pass it repeatedly among themselves

ai.seo_question: What should a poor family do if they only have enough zakat al-fiṭrah for one person?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding zakat al-fiṭrah when a household possesses only enough for one payment. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that it be circulated among the family members so that it counts collectively for them. The narration reflects practical facilitation in fulfilling an act of worship under financial constraint.
